# Cua Driver Bench

Ten desktop tasks on Linux: three across several applications, three of pointer precision, four through an interruption, each checked from the applications' own state; eight of them also in the background, beside a simulated user.

## Options

| Option | Values, default in bold | What it sets | Setups |
|---|---|---|---|
| `desktop_image` | e.g. `cdb-desktop:1`, default `build` | The image each trial's desktop runs: build, the entry's recipe on the bench's public Linux image, made once on the machine; or the name of an image already on the machine (it is not pulled). | yours |
| `desktop_memory` | e.g. `4g`, default `8g` | The most memory each trial's desktop may use, given to the container engine as its memory limit, in gigabytes or megabytes. A program left running in the desktop then cannot take the machine's memory. | yours |
| `max_steps` | e.g. `30`, default `45` | The most acting calls an agent may make on a task: the port's step budget. 45, the bench's limit of 45 turns; the bench counts its own agent's turns, the port counts acting calls. | yours |
| `pause` | e.g. `2.0`, default `1.0` | How long the loop waits after each action before the step's picture is taken, to let the screen settle. 1 second, the pause of the port's conformance kit. | `agent` |

| Option | Value | Refused without (`host`: the driver's machine; `embeddings`: a model the provider serves) |

## Good to know

- Runs any agent that holds the computer port's proof on the bench's tasks. The bench's own launcher runs each trial unchanged and holds its agent's slot open while the agent acts through the port. Each acting call is one step.
- Each task runs under the bench's two conditions as two tasks: ID-foreground, where the agent may take the focus, and ID-background, where a simulated user's window stays in front and types while the agent works. Eight of the ten tasks have a background condition.
- The background's pass is the bench's full one: the task's check passes, the guard sees no violation, and the bench's eight measures show the user undisturbed: key_focus (their keyboard focus), window_raised (a window raised over theirs), typing, pointer, clipboard, space (their workspace), dialog (a dialog on their window) and activation (their window's activation). A measure the bench could not take fails the trial. The trial's page shows the check's own result beside each measure.
- Which tasks: Foreground (10) and Background (8) are the benchmark's own task sets, each run as a job of its own; a run that names no dataset takes Foreground. All tasks (18) lists each task's foreground then its background, side by side. A job of all 18 adds passes of two different measures into one total, so its rate is neither condition's.
- The bench's published comparison runs one fixed agent and model on each computer-use tool. This setup does not repeat that comparison.
- The agent is told the task as the launcher writes it, the name of the computer server, and the bench's two rules as its runner states them: operate only the applications the task names and stay off the network, in about 6 minutes and at most 45 turns.
- Each task has 6 minutes from the moment it is given, and 45 steps (Steps per task). A task cut by the time, by a run's cap of model calls, or a minute after its loop ended is checked as the desktop then stands; a check that passes at the time limit counts, as in the launcher's own row.
- The guard ends a trial when a terminal stays in front for three samples or starts outside the launcher. The desktop's panel shows a terminal launcher.
- Attempts are the bench's trials: attempt k is the launcher's run index k - 1, which sets the seed. Five attempts are the bench's five trials of a task.
- A trial the launcher marks as a harness error is no one's result; --retries runs it again with the same seed, as the bench does.
- A trial whose desktop stops working while it runs is not counted against the agent, and --retries runs it again.
- Desktop image: build makes it once on the machine from the bench's public Linux image and its own provisioning scripts, about 3.5 GB of downloads; or name an image the machine holds.
- Nothing of the bench is copied into Nullius: the install fetches it at its pinned commit, and each trial copies its folder into the desktop. The bench is under FSL-1.1-MIT.

## Upstream limitations

- The bench's scripted solutions of its seven BenchLab tasks run on Hyprland and Windows alone. No reference run shows that each task can be passed on this desktop.
- The desktop's build installs the latest Google Chrome and GnuCash. A later build can differ from the one a score was made with.

## Nullius limitations

- An agent that acts through the port's pointer and keyboard alone disturbs the simulated user at its first pointer or key action (the real pointer moves, or the keys land in the user's window), and so passes no background task. The background suits an agent with a driver that acts on a window behind; the port lets such a driver be sent and started before the task, and its start is measured like any other input.
- The port cannot enforce the bench's rule of acting through the screen alone. A step's code runs as the desktop's user, who can read the task's checker and the trial's files, write an application's store and use sudo. The guard still ends a trial on a terminal. The trial's records list every action's code.
- The bench's scan of its agent's tool calls for code that runs outside the screen does not run here. It reads a transcript that an agent through the port does not write.
- The bench counts its own agent's turns, those with no action included; the port counts acting calls. 45 steps can therefore be more model turns than the bench's 45.
- The 6 minutes start when the task is given, once the agent has started; the bench's own runner counts its agent's start in them.
- The first build of the desktop can take hours on a slow link; a unit's setup may take 4 hours for it.
- A named image is one the machine holds, by a local name of at most 64 characters, with no registry path.
- Each trial's desktop has no network. The task with a local site serves it inside the desktop.
- On the local backend an agent runs as you and can write where you can, the trial's records included.
- When a run stops without removing a trial's desktop, after a Stop too, a process of the desktop's own removes it. A desktop whose process was killed as well stays running; each desktop has the job's label.
